claim: SCOPE adapts a Lean-theorem-proving-oriented model to emit three structured feedback fields (subgoals, gap analysis, robustness checklist) for code generation, trained via SFT plus process-aligned RL with dense structured-critique and sparse execution-score rewards.
scope_conditions: LiveCodeBench V6 and BigCodeBench (Hard), submitted July 2026
quoted_support: We present SCOPE, a prover-initialized subgoal critic for code generation. SCOPE adapts a Lean-oriented prover model to produce three parseable feedback fields for downstream code generation: subgoals, gap analysis, and a robustness checklist.
numbers: LiveCodeBench V6: SCOPE 39.4% pass@1 vs Reflexion 36.6% vs coder-only 20.6%
BigCodeBench (Hard): SCOPE 42.6% vs Reflexion 36.5% vs coder-only 34.5%

claim: SCOPE's improvement over baselines is concentrated specifically in tasks with concrete semantic constraints, and its code corrections are more localized than Reflexion's unstructured critique.
stance_target: value of requirement/subgoal-decomposed feedback for targeted repair
quoted_support: Further analysis shows that SCOPE's gains are concentrated in tasks with concrete semantic constraints and that its code corrections are more localized than Reflexion's.

claim: Existing feedback-based code generation methods rely on unstructured critique or raw execution signals that do not explicitly identify which semantic requirement the code is missing.
quoted_support: Existing feedback-based methods improve over coder-only generation, but they often rely on unstructured critique or execution signals that do not explicitly identify what the code is semantically missing.

claim: SCOPE decomposes specifications into LLM/prover-generated subgoals rather than the actual per-unit-test requirement structure, and treats subgoals uniformly with no confidence-ranked prioritization of which subgoal deserves more inference-time compute.
stance_target: residual novelty of confidence-triggered per-requirement compute allocation (candidate b/d) even after SCOPE
scope_conditions: as described in SCOPE abstract, July 2026
quoted_support: SCOPE, a prover-initialized subgoal critic for code generation.
